title: Inheritance & Polymorphism
description: Reuse through inheritance, many forms, abstract classes, interfaces.

questions.explanation: The variable is Animal but the object is Dog — the object's method wins.

questions.prompt: Why does @Override cause a compile error here?
options: The signature doesn't match the parent's speak()
questions.explanation: @Override asks the compiler to verify — and the extra parameter means it's not an override.

questions.prompt: Order these from most general to most specific.
questions.explanation: LivingThing → Animal → Mammal → Dog, top of the tree to the leaf.

questions.prompt: Which JavaScript is the same override?
questions.explanation: JS needs no @Override — a same-named method in the subclass just overrides.
Dynamic dispatch: the Square object runs Square's area() → 4*4 = 16.0.

options: A class can extend only one parent — use implements for Flyable
questions.explanation: One extends max. The fix: class Bird extends Animal implements Flyable.

questions.prompt: An interface is ___ , so a class provides all the method bodies.
questions.explanation: implements signs the contract — and you can sign more than one.

questions.prompt: Which Java shows the same polymorphism?
questions.code:
const pets = [new Dog(), new Cat()];
for (const p of pets) p.speak();
options:
Animal[] pets = {new Dog(), new Cat()};
for (Animal p : pets) p.speak();
questions.explanation: One Animal-typed loop, many behaviors — polymorphism in both languages.
